title: staged attention pipeline: tiled flash kernel + async KV spill + fused rotary microkernel
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: tails on long-context workloads (8k-32k tokens) show two dominant costs: attention kernel memory pressure and blocking KV management during cache overflow. This PR introduces a staged attention pipeline that (1) tiles attention into multi-stage ops to keep compute on fast paths for common sequence shapes, (2) provides an async KV spill path to host memory for oversized contexts to avoid blocking the inference thread, and (3) ships a small fused rotary/rope microkernel that reduces per-token assembly overhead for rotary embeddings. What changed: - New CU kernel: runtime/attn/staged_flash_kernel.cu implementing tiled Flash-like attention with stage boundaries (qk tile, softmax tile, out tile) and explicit small-size microkernels for rotary application. - Scheduler: runtime/scheduler/hetero_batcher.cpp adds heterogeneous batch splitting so long sequences are split into staged sub-requests and routed to the tiled kernel; includes continuous-batching hooks to merge short requests while preserving latency SLOs. - KV cache: runtime/kv/async_spill.cpp and kv/host_serialization.h implement an async spill-to-host path with lock-free handoff to an IO worker thread and LRU hinting to avoid noisy eviction. - API surface: minor flags to the model config (staged_attention: on/off, kv_spill_threshold) and runtime feature gates. - Tests/benchmarks: tests/attn/perf_long_context.py, benchmarks/long_context/* and microbenchmarks for the rotary microkernel. - Docs: docs/perf/attn_staging.md describing operation and tuning knobs. Key design notes: - The tiled kernel is optimized for sequence lengths where max(seq_len) > 1024; it falls back to the existing fused Flash path for small sequences to avoid regressions. - Async KV spill is bounded: we surface per-request mem usage and backpressure; when the host queue is saturated requests fall back to a best-effort KV truncation policy. - The rotary microkernel was implemented as an in-register fused op to avoid an extra memory pass; it targets float16/AMP paths and has guardrails for fp32. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for tiled kernel correctness (small matrices) - [x] Integration tests with scheduler split/merge logic - [x] End-to-end perf harness runs on p4d and g5 instances - [x] Backwards compatibility: feature gated and off by default for existing models - [x] Docs and release notes added Risks and mitigations: - Memory regression on some models: mitigated by staged_attention=false toggle and automatic fallback on OOM. - Race in KV spill handoff: leveraged lock-free queue and added deterministic reproduction test. - Accuracy drift due to tiling numeric order: validated against reference single-kernel attention on representative prompt sets and added tolerance checks. Rollout plan: deploy to canary fleet with staged_attention enabled for a small percentage of traffic, collect latency and quality regressions, then graduate to general availability depending on metrics in ENG-4821. Notes: this is intentionally conservative in kernel fusion (we only fuse rotary+apply in the microkernel) to make future integration with advanced Flash variants simpler.
commits: staged-attn: add staged flash tiled kernel and microkernel entry points
scheduler: heterogeneous batch splitter and continuous-batching hooks
kv: async host-spill worker and serialization helpers
flags: add staged_attention config and kv_spill_threshold
tests: perf harness and unit tests for staged attention and spill path
docs: perf writeup and tuning guide
review_thread: Ethan Cole: This looks promising, can you add a fast-path switch so we don't hit extra register pressure for <512 sequences?
Priya Nair: Added a short-seq fast-path to route back to existing fused kernel if max_seq < 512; updated config and tests.
Jordan Kim: KV spill path needs a hard cap to avoid OOM storms on host memory. Suggest exposing kv_spill_threshold and queue_depth limits.
Priya Nair: Exposed kv_spill_threshold and host_spill_queue_depth; added saturation behavior and metrics; added e2e test that asserts backpressure behavior.
María Alvarez: Benchmarks show 18% token/sec win on 16k context for decoder-only models but 2% regression on short seqs—acceptable if gated.
Priya Nair: Confirmed short-seq regression is eliminated by short-seq fast-path; added canary rollout plan to release notes.
ci_checks: ci/perf-bench: pass on p4d with benchmarks attached
benchmarks: 16k context, decoder-only (g5.48x): +22% throughput vs baseline Flash v2, 14% lower p95 latency for steady-state batches
8k context, mixed batch sizes: +12% throughput, p95 improved 9%
<512 seq: on-par with baseline when short-seq fast-path enabled (0-2% variance)
release_notes:
- Introduce staged attention pipeline: tiled flash kernel + rotary microkernel + async KV spill (feature gated).
- Default: disabled. Opt-in via model config (staged_attention=true).
- Improvements: significant throughput gains for long-context workloads (8k-32k).
- Notes: monitor kv_spill_host_queue_depth metrics when enabling.
